title: Your Inner Furnace
text: Beneath your skin, an invisible furnace burns day and night without a single break.
nxt: Your body works relentlessly to hold an internal temperature of around thirty-seven degrees Celsius.

title: The Brain Thermostat
text: The control room for this furnace is a small region deep in your brain called the hypothalamus.
nxt: It works like a thermostat, comparing the blood temperature it senses with a target and sending out orders to correct any difference.

title: A Summer Afternoon
text: Think about an ordinary summer afternoon. You step outside, and the blazing sun wraps around your shoulders.
nxt: Your forehead begins to glisten with tiny beads of sweat, and your heart beats a little faster.

nxt: Almost every process keeping you alive relies on specialized proteins called enzymes.

title: The Heart Below 28

nxt: The rhythm of the heartbeat depends on chemical pumps moving ions across cell membranes, and cold disrupts them.

title: Not Dead Until Warm
text: Why do physicians repeat that phrase? Because profound cold is a double-edged sword.
nxt: It paralyzes cell function, but it also dramatically slows metabolism.

title: Not Dead Until Warm
text: At very low temperatures, brain cells need far less oxygen to survive. One famous case happened in Norway in 1999.

title: Not Dead Until Warm
text: A young doctor and skier named Anna Bågenholm fell through the ice of a frozen stream and was trapped beneath it for about eighty minutes.

title: Not Dead Until Warm
text: By the time rescuers reached her, her core temperature had dropped to about thirteen point seven degrees Celsius and her heart had stopped.

title: Not Dead Until Warm
text: Doctors warmed her blood outside the body, and she recovered.
nxt: Cases like hers are rare, and each one depends on many lucky details, but they show why doctors do not give up on a cold patient too soon.

title: The Fourteen-Degree Window
text: So where do the boundaries of human survival lie?

title: The Fourteen-Degree Window
text: A window of roughly fourteen degrees Celsius separates a living body from the edge of death.
nxt: There are rare survivors outside that window, but it is a useful picture of how narrow our margin really is.

title: Beyond Biology
text: How did we conquer the planet with such a fragile furnace inside us? The secret is that humans never relied on biology alone.

title: Beyond Biology
text: Polar bears evolved thick blubber, and desert foxes grew large, heat-radiating ears.
nxt: Our ancestors developed tools, culture, and cooperation.

title: Cities as Life Support
text: Every city you see today, from the freezing streets of northern capitals to the scorching desert metropolises, is a life-support system.

title: Cities as Life Support

title: The Hidden Balancing Act

title: The Hidden Balancing Act
text: Your skin adjusts its moisture, your lungs release excess heat with every breath, and your brain keeps calculating what your body needs.

title: The Hidden Balancing Act
text: You never have to command your sweat glands to open. Your body manages this delicate dance automatically, second by second, without your awareness.

title: A Delicate Balance
text: We often imagine strength as something rugged and unyielding, like stone, steel, or mountains. But life is not rigid like stone.

title: A Delicate Balance
text: Human life is a dynamic balance, dancing on the edge between burning up and freezing over.
nxt: We are fragile creatures made mostly of warm water and soft proteins, yet that very fragility drove us to invent, build, and explore.

title: A Delicate Balance
